usage.describe: A research grouping for packaged everyday goods: food, drink, household and personal care products, and the retailers that sell them. Durable goods, clothing and restaurants are outside it. All links are hypotheses to investigate.

sector_node.describe: Sector-wide links generate candidate exposures only; verify company applicability and materiality.

branches.question: Which macro conditions change what households can spend, what the group's foreign sales are worth, or how its steady earnings are valued?
Which rules change what a product costs to bring to the shelf, or whether it may be sold as it is?
What moves the cost of making and selling the goods, and how long does a shock last?
Who sets the price on the shelf, and who keeps the margin when costs or demand change?
Are households buying less, buying cheaper, buying elsewhere, or is the channel only changing its stock?

concepts.label: Household income
concepts.description_lead: What households have to spend after prices rise

concepts.label: Rates
concepts.description_lead: What steady dividends and cash flows are valued against
observables_to_research: the group's dividend yield against the 10-year Treasury yield

related_concepts.question: Is the group repricing with real yields while its sales are unchanged?

concepts.label: Currency
concepts.description_lead: Translates foreign sales and prices imported inputs

concepts.label: Risk appetite
concepts.description_lead: Whether investors are seeking or shedding risk
observables_to_research: the group's return against the broad market over the same sessions
concepts.observable_with: Investor intent is not published. Implied-volatility term structure and the group's relative return stand in for it, on the assumption that a rush to steady earners shows up in both.

related_concepts.question: Was the volatility term structure signalling market-wide stress when the group moved against the market?
Had the group's own trend broken, or only the market's?

concepts.label: Trade rules
concepts.description_lead: Tariffs, quotas and embargoes on inputs, finished goods and farm exports
observables_to_research: tariff schedules and their effective dates

concepts.label: Product rules
concepts.description_lead: What may be sold, how it is labelled and taxed, and when it is recalled
observables_to_research: ingredient and labelling rules with effective dates

concepts.label: Harvest and herd shocks
concepts.description_lead: Weather and disease that cut a crop or a herd
observables_to_research: official crop condition and yield reports

concepts.label: Agricultural commodities
concepts.description_lead: Crops and livestock products bought as ingredients
observables_to_research: prices of grains, sugar, coffee, cocoa, edible oils, dairy and meat

concepts.label: Energy, packaging and freight
concepts.description_lead: What it costs to make, wrap and move the goods

concepts.label: Labour
concepts.description_lead: Wages in factories, warehouses and stores
observables_to_research: average hourly earnings in retail and in food manufacturing

concepts.label: Branded manufacturers
concepts.description_lead: Make packaged everyday goods and sell them under their own brands
observables_to_research: organic sales growth split into volume, price and mix
gross margin and its stated drivers

concepts.label: Retailers
concepts.description_lead: Sell everyday goods to households and decide what is on the shelf
observables_to_research: comparable sales split into transactions and average ticket

concepts.label: Store brands
concepts.description_lead: Goods a retailer sells under its own name beside the brands
observables_to_research: retailers' reported own-brand share of sales
the price gap between store brands and brands
concepts.observable_with: Share by category comes from scanner data sold to subscribers. In public, only what individual retailers and manufacturers choose to report is available, so a retailer's own figure stands in for the market's.

concepts.label: Household demand
concepts.description_lead: How much households buy, of what quality, and where
observables_to_research: official retail sales of food and household goods
trading down, pack-size and channel commentary
concepts.observable_with: Official retail sales are in money, not units, and mix price with volume. Volumes are published only by companies for their own products, so both are partial readings.

concepts.label: Channel inventory
concepts.description_lead: Stock held by retailers and distributors between factory and shopper
observables_to_research: manufacturers' comments on customer stock levels
shipments against sales to shoppers where both are reported
concepts.observable_with: A manufacturer's stock sitting in its customers' warehouses is not published. Retailers' total inventory and each side's commentary stand in for it.

concepts.label: Population and preferences
concepts.description_lead: Slow changes in how many people buy a category and whether they want it

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: Steady cash flows and dividends are valued against bond yields, so a rise in yields can lower the group's valuation with no change in its sales. In a market sell-off the move to safety can outweigh this.

test_criteria.trigger: The 10-year real yield moves by 25 basis points or more over 20 US sessions while VIX closes below VIX3M on every one of them.
test_criteria.observable: The return of a broad consumer staples fund against SPY over the same 20 sessions.
test_criteria.supports_if: The fund lags SPY when the real yield rose, or leads it when the yield fell.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The fund leads SPY when the real yield rose, or lags it when the yield fell.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: When investors cut risk, money moves toward companies whose sales hold up, so the group tends to fall less than a falling market and rise less than a rising one.

test_criteria.trigger: VIX closes above VIX3M after at least 20 sessions below it.
test_criteria.observable: The return of a broad consumer staples fund and of SPY over the following 20 US sessions.
test_criteria.supports_if: SPY falls over the window and the fund's return is higher than SPY's.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: SPY falls over the window and the fund's return is lower than SPY's. A window in which SPY rises settles nothing.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: Currency moves change the reported value of sales made abroad and the cost of imported inputs. The net effect depends on where a company sells and where it makes and buys.

test_criteria.trigger: A company reports a quarter in which the US dollar's average value against its main foreign currencies differs by 5% or more from the same quarter a year earlier.
test_criteria.observable: The effect of currency on sales growth that the company itself states for that quarter, for the whole company. The gap between reported and organic growth is not used: it also holds acquisitions and disposals.
test_criteria.supports_if: The stated currency effect has the sign the dollar's move implies and is at least one percentage point.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The stated currency effect is under half a percentage point or has the opposite sign. If the company does not disclose this figure for that scope, the assessment is inconclusive.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: When real income falls, households go on buying necessities but trade down to cheaper brands, smaller packs or store brands, and cut the categories they can do without first.

test_criteria.trigger: Official real disposable personal income is lower than a year earlier for two consecutive quarters.
test_criteria.observable: One branded manufacturer's volume, for the whole company, in those quarters and the next. A retailer's store-brand share is a different measure and belongs to the store-brand lead.
test_criteria.window: Those two quarters and the next.
test_criteria.supports_if: The manufacturer's volume is lower than a year earlier in at least one of the three quarters.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The manufacturer's volume is unchanged or higher than a year earlier in all three quarters. If the company does not disclose this figure for that scope, the assessment is inconclusive.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: Population growth, ageing and changing views on health move a category's volume slowly and for a long time. Price can cover a falling volume for a while, not indefinitely.

Repeat purchase of necessities makes volumes far steadier than those of durable goods, so a manufacturer's sales change more through price, substitution and population than through the business cycle.

Households change where they shop as well as what they buy, moving toward discounters, larger packs and fewer trips when budgets tighten. A retailer positioned on low prices can gain shoppers in a downturn while others lose them.

test_criteria.trigger: Official real disposable personal income is lower than a year earlier for two consecutive quarters.
test_criteria.observable: The transactions component of comparable sales at one retailer positioned on low prices, for its home market.
test_criteria.window: Those two quarters and the next.
test_criteria.supports_if: Transactions are higher than a year earlier in at least two of the three quarters.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: Transactions are lower than a year earlier in at least two of the three quarters. Any other outcome is inconclusive, as is a retailer that does not report transactions.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: Weather or disease cuts supply, and the price rises and stays high until a new crop or herd is grown, which takes from one season to several years depending on the product. A producer that itself lost output sells less at the higher price.

test_criteria.trigger: An official report cuts the estimated supply of a named crop or animal product by 5% or more because of weather or disease.
test_criteria.observable: The price of that product, and the time until official supply estimates return to their level before the cut.
test_criteria.window: From the report until supply estimates recover, or two years, whichever is sooner.
test_criteria.supports_if: The price is higher three months after the report than before it and does not return to its earlier level before supply recovers.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The price is back at or below its earlier level within three months while official supply estimates are still reduced.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: A tariff or embargo that closes an export market leaves more of a crop at home and lowers its domestic price, which helps the companies that buy it and hurts the farmers who grow it.
Tariffs and quotas raise the cost of imported inputs and finished goods. Who bears it depends on whether the importer can change source, and on whether its customers accept a higher price.

test_criteria.trigger: A tariff on a named input or product category takes effect on a stated date.
test_criteria.observable: What one company that states it imports the item says the tariff cost it, as an amount or as an effect on margin. Its total gross margin is not used: savings elsewhere can hide the cost.
test_criteria.window: The four fiscal quarters after the effective date.
test_criteria.supports_if: The company states a cost from the tariff, or states that it changed source or raised a price because of it.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The company states that the tariff had no material effect on its costs. If it says neither, or does not say whether it imports the item, the assessment is inconclusive.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: A rule on ingredients, labelling or sale, a tax on a specific product, or a recall can remove a product, raise its cost or move demand to a substitute. The effect belongs to the category, and a competitor without the affected product can gain.

A rise in ingredient prices reaches cost of goods with a delay set by hedges, supply contracts and inventory. Margins fall until prices are raised, and recover beyond their old level if those prices hold after the ingredient falls back.

test_criteria.trigger: The price of an ingredient a company names as material is 20% or more above its level a year earlier.
test_criteria.observable: The effect of commodity or input costs on gross margin that the company itself states, for the whole company. Total gross margin is not used: pricing and savings move it too.
test_criteria.window: The four fiscal quarters after the price first meets the trigger.
test_criteria.supports_if: The stated effect of input costs on gross margin is negative in at least one of the four quarters.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The stated effect of input costs on gross margin is zero or positive in all four quarters. If the company does not disclose this figure for that scope, the assessment is inconclusive.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: Energy, packaging materials and freight are costs every product carries, so they move margins across categories at once, with the same delay from contracts and hedges as ingredients.
Wages are the largest cost of running stores and warehouses that a retailer controls, so faster wage growth lowers its margin unless prices, productivity or sales per store rise with it.

A large retailer decides what is on the shelf, and can refuse a price increase, demand promotion money or remove a product. How far it can push depends on whether shoppers will go elsewhere for the brand.

test_criteria.trigger: A branded manufacturer announces a list-price increase of a stated size for a segment.
test_criteria.observable: The pricing component of sales growth the manufacturer then reports for that segment. One retailer refusing the increase is evidence about that account only and does not settle this test.
test_criteria.window: The two fiscal quarters after the increase takes effect.
test_criteria.supports_if: The reported pricing component is below the announced increase by a percentage point or more in both quarters, and the manufacturer attributes the shortfall to its retail customers.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: The reported pricing component is at or above the announced increase in at least one of the two quarters. A shortfall the manufacturer does not attribute to customers is inconclusive, as is a manufacturer that reports no separate pricing component.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: A price increase raises revenue per unit and loses some volume. How much is lost depends on how strongly shoppers want the brand and how close the substitutes are, so the same increase can pay for one product and not for another.

test_criteria.trigger: A branded manufacturer reports a pricing component of sales growth five percentage points or more above a year earlier for a segment in a fiscal quarter. A combined price-and-mix figure does not qualify: it can rise because shoppers bought different products.
test_criteria.observable: The volume component reported for the same segment in the same quarter and the next.
test_criteria.supports_if: Volume for that segment is lower than a year earlier in at least one of the two quarters.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: Volume for that segment is unchanged or higher than a year earlier in both quarters. A company that reports price and mix together, or no volume for the segment, is inconclusive.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: A retailer chooses how much shelf its own brand gets and how far below the brand it is priced. It earns more on its own brand and can use it to press a supplier, but it loses shoppers if they came for the brand.

A store brand gives households a cheaper substitute and gives the retailer a product it earns more on and controls. Share moves to store brands when the price gap widens or incomes fall, and part of it stays after the cause has passed.

test_criteria.trigger: A retailer reports a rise in own-brand share of sales of one percentage point or more from a year earlier.
test_criteria.observable: The same retailer's own-brand share of sales, on the same definition, one year after that report. A manufacturer's volume is a different scope and does not settle this test: the retailer's share can rise while one supplier's volume is flat.
test_criteria.window: The four fiscal quarters after the report.
test_criteria.supports_if: A year later the share is still at least half a percentage point above its level before the rise.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: A year later the share is at or below its level before the rise. A share between the two is inconclusive, as is a retailer that stops reporting it or changes the definition.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: A manufacturer records a sale when it ships to a retailer or distributor, so a channel that cuts its stock lowers reported sales below what households are buying, and restocking lifts them above it.

test_criteria.trigger: A manufacturer, or a retailer that is a large customer, reports that the retailer is reducing its inventory.
test_criteria.observable: For one manufacturer and one stated set of products, its shipment growth against the growth in sales to shoppers reported for the same products and the same quarters.
test_criteria.window: The fiscal quarter of the report and the next.
test_criteria.supports_if: Shipment growth is below the growth in sales to shoppers in at least one of the two quarters.
test_criteria.contradicts_if: Shipment growth is at or above the growth in sales to shoppers in both quarters. Where the two are not reported for the same products, the assessment is inconclusive.
